arecel_reference.citation: Wang et al., Are We Ready For Learned Cardinality Estimation?, PVLDB 14(9), 1640-1654 (2021), doi:10.14778/3461535.3461552

scientific_question: Within each dataset, do independently calibrated Nominal and PESS policies choose pairwise-MCV extstats sets with different PostgreSQL cardinality-estimation generalization on a prospectively frozen query cohort that was not used for resource selection? Empty is a matched baseline.

scope.unit: single-table conjunctive COUNT(*) query; query has one or more predicates and may have more than two
scope.cross_dataset_policy: calibrate and optimize independently for each table; no coefficients, candidate objects, or selected sets transfer across unrelated schemas
scope.joint_robust: excluded unless researcher separately approves and documents D-007 shared-policy assumptions

candidate_universe.freeze_source: exact labeled pairs and order in Issue #59 protocol-v1.json; copy and SHA-pin into the eventual execution manifest before calibration or held-out outcomes
candidate_universe.interpretation: bounded prospective candidate universe inherited from the outcome-free Issue #59 audit, not exhaustive over all column pairs and not proof of physical payload or planner use

calibration_and_selection.calibration_source: within-dataset development/calibration queries only; query structures and labels available to calibration are frozen and hashed before selection
calibration_and_selection.test_firewall: selection code receives candidate universe, validation calibration records and budgets only; it must not receive test SQL literals, test truth, test estimates, PostgreSQL test traces, or post-selection feedback
calibration_and_selection.model: use the corrected natural-log definitions and exact Nominal/PESS objectives reviewed in PR #58; do not use defective formal-v4 coefficients; pin source commit, inputs and objective implementation before selection
calibration_and_selection.nominal_scheme: deterministic greedy maximal matching in frozen candidate order, as a scoped mathematical policy definition only
calibration_and_selection.pess_scheme: all maximal matchings of the selected task graph; maximal is not maximum-cardinality; task-wise worst loss remains the frozen PESS objective
calibration_and_selection.loss: positive pre-clamp absolute natural-log error under the reviewed frozen model; optimizer objective is not the held-out evaluation metric

resource_budget.meaning: additive candidate-count proxy only; not physical Maint or ANALYZE time
resource_budget.infeasible: report INFEASIBLE; never substitute a neighboring budget

ties.optimization: enumerate/report every objective-optimal unordered resource set
ties.deployed_set: lexicographically smallest sorted tuple of candidate IDs among optimal sets; records all tied alternatives
ties.pg_creation_order: ascending frozen candidate index, separately recorded; does not redefine the unordered optimizer decision

cohort_and_independence.legacy_arecel_test: not fresh held-out evidence: prior Stage 1A/Stage 2B outcomes and selection exposure prohibit reuse as the primary prospective cohort
cohort_and_independence.prospective_source_proposal: new deterministic AreCEL-style single-table query generation per dataset, with a published seed/algorithm and separately generated development/calibration and test pools; generate predicate counts 1..number_of_columns and supported equality/open-range/closed-range operators, with both in-domain and out-of-domain centers
cohort_and_independence.group_split: assign normalized predicate-template SHA-256 groups to development/calibration/test before generating or opening cardinality labels; entire groups belong to exactly one split
cohort_and_independence.historical_overlap: compare exact-SQL and normalized-template fingerprints against all available historical split/cohort manifests, including exposed Stage 1A/#48 cohorts; report group and query counts plus split-pair overlap; reject contaminated groups without consulting labels
cohort_and_independence.test_freeze: freeze cohort IDs, SQL/template hashes, generator/version/seed, cohort size, stratum counts and input hashes before opening any test truth or estimate
cohort_and_independence.proposed_minimum: at least 1000 unique test template groups per dataset for an interpretable P95; P99/Max remain tail-descriptive; at least two datasets must pass all gates for cross-dataset replication language
cohort_and_independence.insufficient: if fresh template-disjoint cohorts cannot be formed or minimum size is not met, BLOCKED/INCONCLUSIVE; do not fall back to exposed legacy test outcomes

primary.name: per-dataset P95 Q-error with one-row floor (Q1)
primary.formula: Q1(E,A)=max(E,A,1)/max(min(E,A),1), for finite E>=0 and A>=0
primary.quantile: nearest-rank empirical quantile, rank=ceil(0.95*n), after averaging log(Q1) across paired physical sample replicates within query and exponentiating; no pooling across datasets
primary.contrast: paired per-query log(Q1_PESS)-log(Q1_Nominal), with Empty shown separately; uncertainty resamples normalized template groups, not plans or repetitions
primary.pairwise_classification: with two sample replicates, compare exact rational arithmetic means of the two per-replicate Q1 values: benefit iff PESS<Nominal, harm iff PESS>Nominal, tie iff equal; no floating tolerance. Report the paired mean-log-Q1 delta separately.
primary.adaptation_note: Q1 is an explicit one-row floor adaptation, not exactly AreCEL's natural positive-domain Q-error

secondary: per-dataset P50/P99/Max Q1 with the same aggregation rule
natural AreCEL Q-error max(E,A)/min(E,A) on E>0 and A>0 only, with eligible n and coverage reported; zero/nonpositive cases are never silently folded into this subset
counts of exact-zero agreement (E=0,A=0), estimate-only zero, truth-only zero, and invalid/nonfinite/negative values
mean absolute positive pre-clamp log error on its explicitly defined positive domain, as continuity with the model metric; keep distinct from clamped/rounded Plan Rows
per-query PESS-vs-Nominal Q1 and log-Q1 deltas; benefit/harm/tie classification uses exact rational Q1 comparison, no floating tolerance
Empty/Nominal/PESS outcomes reported separately for every dataset and budget; no pooled primary statistic

strata.rule: strata are descriptive and predeclared; never drop an unfavorable query because its syntactic graph, payload or trace differs from the model

postgresql_physical_evaluation.comparison: for each dataset/budget, evaluate Empty and each selected Nominal/PESS unordered set; deduplicate identical sets but retain policy labels; paired query IDs across all treatments
postgresql_physical_evaluation.same_conditions: same pinned PG 16.14 instrumented build/flags, table bytes/schema/import, GUCs, statistics target, ANALYZE sampling protocol, query text, session settings and resource limits within a dataset; isolate each treatment database and randomize/counterbalance treatment build order
postgresql_physical_evaluation.sample_gate: prove the sample is identical across paired treatments, or explicitly treat independent sample realizations as a blocking factor and report their identity; if sample comparability cannot be established, BLOCKED for the primary paired interpretation
postgresql_physical_evaluation.creation_order: create selected objects in frozen ascending candidate index; record object definition, catalog OID, creation order, payload presence/usable MCV contents and per-query selected OIDs/clause mapping
postgresql_physical_evaluation.coverage: separately classify syntactic candidate availability, usable MCV payload, selected-stat OID trace, claimed clause indexes and trace completeness; EXPLAIN rows alone do not prove selected objects
postgresql_physical_evaluation.mismatch: retain and report queries where actual PG behavior is outside the prescribed matching assumptions; do not reinterpret them as a matching or exclude them from overall Q-error
postgresql_physical_evaluation.failure_policy: missing payload/trace, invalid row estimate, measurement error or budget/time cap hit is a reported failure/coverage state; no silent replacement query or method-specific deletion

prospective_caps.datasets: up to four; minimum two pass all gates for cross-dataset replication
prospective_caps.wall_time_budget: proposed hard cap 24 elapsed hours per dataset including import, ANALYZE, query trace and reruns; confirm hardware feasibility before authorization
prospective_caps.disk_budget: proposed hard cap 100 GiB total disposable runtime data; confirm available capacity before authorization
prospective_caps.reruns: only predeclared infrastructure failures may be retried once; retain failed attempt and reason; no outcome-driven reruns
prospective_caps.stop: stop a dataset at first violated integrity/resource cap; mark BLOCKED/INCONCLUSIVE and do not expand scope
